chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Zakariyya ibn 'Amr, from a man, from Isma'il ibn Jabir, who said:

A righteous man said to me: 'Do not expose yourself to the rights [of others], be patient with the calamity, and do not give your brother from yourself that which harms you more than it benefits him.'
ai.seo_question: What are the key ethical principles regarding giving and patience in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from the chapter on rentals (Ijarat) in Tahdhib al-Ahkam emphasizes the principle of 'la darar wa la dirar' (no harm) in social transactions, advising believers to balance generosity with self-preservation. It highlights the Shia scholarly focus on prudence in financial and interpersonal dealings, ensuring that one's obligations do not lead to personal ruin.
